proposal: The Mandate recommends making performance appraisal meaningful (it criticizes ratings clustered at the top, wants political executives to take an active role in supervising career appraisals, and wants managers judged on how they rate staff) and reissuing the 2018 order (EO 13839) that shortened improvement periods, sped discipline, required reminders to supervisors about expiring probationary periods, and barred settlements that alter personnel records. It also proposes simplifying the appeals structure with the MSPB as the main reviewer of adverse actions.

Statutory merit pay or a government-wide pay-for-performance system, which the Mandate says needs a reform-friendly Congress
Consolidating employee appeals at the MSPB (EEOC federal-sector function moved to MSPB; OSC investigative functions returned to OPM): no such action found

review.mandate_note: Pages 73 to 76 criticize ratings clustered at the top, want managers judged on how they rate staff and political executives active in career appraisals, call for reissuing EO 13839, and propose making the MSPB the main reviewer of adverse actions; EO 13839's probationary provision was a reminder to supervisors about expiring probationary periods, so 'tightened probationary reviews' is reworded.

source_checks.note: OPM final rule published 2026-07-07 (91 FR 41521), effective 2026-08-06, compliance date 2027-01-01 for summary-level provisions: removes the bar on standardized distribution (intended for Levels 4 and 5), drops Level 2, removes ratings of record from negotiated grievances as agreements expire, requires a supervisory critical element.

OPM Director memo dated 2026-09-21: combined Level 4 and 5 ratings capped at 40 percent of each career SES, SP and GS population for periods ending 2026-09-30, waivers up to 50 percent; conflicting CBA provisions continue until the agreement expires.

OPM and MSPB proposed rule published 2026-07-02 (91 FR 40444), comments to 2026-08-03 and later reopened: 30-day improvement period, removal as default penalty, no required progressive discipline, no record-altering settlements, MSPB drops Douglas factors; relies on EO 13839 and says its policies were restored in 2025.

significance.rationale: Faster removals, tougher appraisals and a simplified appeals path would materially change job protections across the federal workforce.

status_summary: OPM finalized two appraisal rules: the Senior Executive Service rule (published 2025-09-15, effective 2025-10-15) and the General Schedule rule (published 2026-07-07, effective 2026-08-06, with some summary-level provisions required from 2027-01-01). Both let OPM set a distribution of top ratings; the General Schedule rule also drops Level 2 and removes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures as agreements expire. An OPM memo of 2026-09-21 caps combined Level 4 and 5 ratings at 40 percent of each covered career population for appraisal periods ending 2026-09-30, with waivers up to 50 percent. The removal-side changes resembling EO 13839 (a 30-day improvement period, removal as the default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, limits on settlements that alter records) are in a joint OPM and MSPB proposed rule of 2026-07-02 that is not yet final. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB has not happened; OPM-run appeals now handle reductions in force.

timeline.event: OPM memo on revocation of EO 14003 tells agencies to review discipline and performance policies changed under that order and return to first-term policies, with a report due 2025-03-07; it does not itself reinstate EO 13839.

OPM final rule, Assuring Responsive and Accountable Federal Executive Management (effective 2025-10-15), lets OPM set forced distribution of SES rating levels and removes a diversity-related appraisal factor.
OPM announces a final suitability rule extending suitability actions to serious post-appointment misconduct in covered positions (date from OPM news listing; Federal Register citation not reviewed).

OPM and MSPB publish proposed rule Promoting Employee Accountability: default 30-day improvement opportunity, removal as default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, MSPB to drop the Douglas factors, limits on settlement terms that alter records, no official time to represent colleagues in covered proceedings.

OPM final rule on performance appraisal for General Schedule, prevailing rate and certain other employees (effective 2026-08-06): drops Level 2, allows OPM-set distribution of upper ratings, removes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures, requires a supervisory critical element.
OPM releases a Performance Management Officer manual and updated appraisal-system approval form to help agencies implement the General Schedule rule.
OPM reopens the Promoting Employee Accountability comment period (to 2026-09-29) limited to new OPM data and a report published 2026-08-27.

OPM memo sets FY2026 standardized distribution: combined Level 4 and 5 ratings capped at 40 percent per covered population (first year for career General Schedule employees), with waivers up to 50 percent, plus awards guidance steering at least 60 percent of bonus pools to Level 4 and 5.

title: Strengthen appraisal ratings and speed removal of poor performers
